factors.finding: Established receiving role: 29 catches for 297 yards and 2 TDs on 43 targets through Week 7; PFF lists 205 routes and a 43.4-yard receiving average over his last five games.
Week 7: four catches for 48 yards and a touchdown; recent five receiving-yard outputs shown by PFF were 26, 42, 64, 37 and 48.

PFF matchup data grades the Panthers' tight-end coverage as a favorable matchup. A separate defensive-by-position source shows Carolina allowing 46.3 TE receiving yards per game through Week 7, near league average rather than an extreme weakness.

Matthew Golden's shoulder/foot status was uncertain and he had missed practice early in the week; if unavailable, targets could redistribute, but the final status was not verified as of this analysis.
Packers at home in a competitive game environment; forecast is clear with light winds and no expected rain.
Kraft's role is steady, but yardage remains dependent on targets and receiving efficiency; the Core line is a modest threshold relative to his recent production.

stage3_context.implication: Strongest contextual profile among the candidates: stable usage, recent production above the Core threshold, and a generally favorable TE matchup. Preserve normal target/short-week variance.

factors.finding: The Panthers' final Week 8 report listed Young as a full participant with no game designation.
Young passed for 163 yards with 1 TD and 2 INTs in the Week 7 43–13 loss to Tampa Bay.

NFL.com's Week 8 preview reports five sacks and pressure on 51.5% of Young's dropbacks in Week 7; Green Bay had generated pressure on 38.5% of dropbacks without blitzing. Carolina also lost RT Taylor Moton for the season, and LG Damien Lewis is out.
Green Bay's defense had 9 interceptions through Week 7, seven generated without blitzing, per NFL.com; this creates pressure and turnover risk.
A close projected game could keep Carolina passing, but sustained pressure or an early deficit could also reduce efficiency and disrupt drives.
Clear, dry conditions and light wind are not expected to materially impede passing.

stage3_context.implication: The passing-yard Core has a plausible volume path but major pass-protection and pressure concerns. Context does not support treating the historical 6/10 as a forecast.

factors.finding: Team-leading 25.6% target share through Week 7 (54 targets reported across six games).
Week 6: six catches for 86 yards; Week 7: four catches for 40 yards on six targets. The latest game cleared neither the 49.5-yard Core nor the 59.5-yard Ceiling.
Green Bay had allowed 156.7 receiving yards per game to wide receivers through Week 7, a relatively permissive position-level figure in the cited dataset.
Young's Week 7 pressure and turnover issues, Taylor Moton's season-ending injury, and Damien Lewis being out can constrain downfield passing and sustained drives.
McMillan is the lead target, but Coker and tight ends remain part of the target distribution; yardage output has varied substantially across recent games.
No meaningful wind or precipitation concern is forecast.

stage3_context.implication: Primary Carolina receiving option by target share, but quarterback pressure limits confidence. Core is more defensible than Ceiling; contextual read remains mixed.

factors.finding: The Panthers' final Week 8 report listed Coker as full participation and without a game designation despite the earlier shoulder issue.
Coker accounted for 18.5% of Carolina's reported targets through Week 7 across five games.
Week 7: one catch for 9 yards on four targets. Usage tracking reports a recent decline in target share and snap share over the last three games versus the earlier comparison window.
Young's pressure problems and losses on the offensive line create a risk to drive success and catch conversion.
Forecast is clear and dry.
Reception count depends on route/snap share and target conversion; Week 7 did not support the Core threshold despite four targets.

stage3_context.implication: Availability is reassuring, but recent production and declining usage are warning signs. The Core reception threshold is not contextually strong enough to upgrade.

factors.finding: 29 receptions on 43 targets through Week 7; PFF lists 205 routes and 6.6 projected targets for this matchup.
Kraft recorded four catches on the way to 48 yards and a touchdown in Week 7.
PFF's matchup analysis identifies Carolina's TE coverage as a favorable matchup; the receptions Core is below the recent typical catch count.
Matthew Golden's status remained uncertain in the early-week reports; a potential absence could alter target distribution, but the final status was not confirmed.
Home game, competitive spread, and benign weather offer no obvious environmental obstacle.
Reception volume is generally less dependent on a single long catch than yardage, but target distribution among Green Bay's receivers remains a factor.

stage3_context.implication: Stable role and recent four-catch game support the 3.5 Core. Context is favorable, while final receiver availability and target competition remain watch items.

factors.finding: Love threw for 274 yards on 45 attempts in Week 7; his previous three games produced 276, 367 and 197 yards. Season total was 1,958 passing yards through seven games.
Love played all 67 offensive snaps in Week 7 and was off the early-week estimated injury report after a prior back issue.

Matthew Golden, who led Green Bay with 36 catches and ranked second with 540 receiving yards, had missed the first two early-week practices with shoulder/foot issues. His final status was not verified at research cutoff.

Green Bay's offensive line is banged up; the NFL preview notes the Packers had not rushed for 100 yards in a game and averaged 2.9 yards per carry, but Carolina's weak run defense could tempt Green Bay to lean on the ground game.
Carolina had allowed 208.2 passing yards per game through Week 7 in the cited defensive-by-position dataset, while Green Bay may have to throw more if its run game remains ineffective.
A competitive game and benign weather are compatible with passing volume.

stage3_context.implication: Recent passing volume and production support the Core, but receiver availability, a short week, and the possibility of a deliberate run-game approach keep the overall context mixed.

records.stage3_exclusion_rationale: Core alternate historical HR is 4/10; available structure does not provide a viable candidate path for later evaluation.
Core alternate historical HR is 5/10 and the ceiling is 3/10; available structure does not provide a sufficiently supported candidate path for later evaluation.

factors.finding: Usage tracking shows Watson with a 21.3% target share through Week 7. He was among the league leaders in receiving touchdowns with six through seven appearances, per the Panthers' official opponent preview.
Week 7: five catches for 57 yards on eight targets, leading Green Bay in receiving yards.

Carolina entered the game with significant cornerback availability problems; the Panthers' official report ruled out Akayleb Evans and the team's preview noted only two healthy cornerbacks at that point.
Watson had been managed with an ankle issue in the prior week; the early-week Packers injury report did not list him, but final Thursday status was not independently confirmed at research cutoff.
Love is active and has recently generated high pass volume; weather is clear with light wind.
Watson's explosive-play role can clear yardage thresholds efficiently, but yardage remains sensitive to depth of target and the number of downfield opportunities.

stage3_context.implication: Role, Week 7 production and Carolina's depleted cornerback group support the Core receiving-yard threshold, with the main uncertainty being short-week availability and volatile big-play dependence.

records.stage3_exclusion_rationale: Core alternate historical HR is 5/10 and ceiling is 5/10; available structure does not provide a sufficiently supported candidate path for later evaluation.

factors.finding: Watson's 21.3% target share through Week 7 and eight Week 7 targets support a repeatable opportunity path.
He caught five of eight targets in Week 7.
Carolina's cornerback depth was depleted entering Thursday's game.
Prior ankle management is noted, though Watson was not listed on the early-week estimated report available at research cutoff; final status was not independently confirmed.
Matthew Golden's potential absence could redirect targets to Watson, but Green Bay has multiple capable receivers and the final status was uncertain.
Clear conditions and light wind create no obvious receiving obstacle.

stage3_context.implication: The 3.5 Core has a clear role-based path from recent target and catch volume. The context is favorable, subject to final availability and target-distribution uncertainty.

factors.finding: The Panthers' final Week 8 report listed Waller as full participation and without a game designation.
Week 7: one catch for 50 yards and a touchdown on two targets; the low yardage threshold was cleared, but the result was driven by one explosive reception.
Waller had a 10.9% target share through Week 7, below McMillan and Coker, and competes with other tight ends and receivers.
Green Bay had allowed only 32.9 tight-end receiving yards per game through Week 7, the lowest figure in the cited defensive-by-position source.
Carolina's pass protection and Young's pressure rate are significant concerns that can disrupt target volume and conversion.
The 9.5-yard Core is a low bar relative to his L10 evidence, but recent production is volatile and the 14.5-yard Ceiling requires another meaningful gain.

stage3_context.implication: The low Core threshold and locked historical HR are supportive, but the modest target share, volatile Week 7 output, difficult TE matchup and Carolina pass-protection concerns make the contextual read mixed.
